intro: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is in Brussels for the EU Enlargement Summit, where he outlined a potential timeline for membership application and discussed economic cooperation. Meanwhile, domestic developments include a central bank rate hike, a high-level anti-corruption case, and new details on a border incident with Azerbaijan.

topics.title: Pashinyan outlines timeline for potential EU membership application
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced during his visit to Brussels that Armenia could apply for EU membership in 2027 or 2028. He discussed Armenia-EU relations, economic cooperation, and energy ties with European officials including European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and EU Commissioner Gert Jan Koopman.

topics.title: Central Bank of Armenia raises policy rate to 7.00%
topics.text: The Central Bank of Armenia increased the policy rate by 0.25 percentage points to 7.00%. Governor Martin Galstyan stated the bank cannot yet assess the potential impact of a projected gas price rise, while noting that Russian currency restrictions are unlikely to significantly affect Armenian citizens or Russian relocators.

topics.title: Anti-Corruption Committee launches criminal case against Hayk Sargsyan
topics.text: The Anti-Corruption Committee has initiated criminal proceedings against Hayk Sargsyan and transferred the case to the Investigative Committee. In a separate budgetary move, the Prime Minister's Office budget was cut by AMD 1.656 billion.

topics.title: Conflicting narratives emerge on Azerbaijani soldier border crossing
topics.text: Top Armenian security officials stated that an Azerbaijani serviceman who breached the border near Shaki had no intent to kill. The Investigative Committee chairman corroborated this assessment, while Azerbaijan was separately ordered by a court to compensate the family of a killed Armenian serviceman.

topics.title: Armenia confirms readiness for reciprocal lawsuit withdrawal after peace deal
topics.text: Armenian officials confirmed the country is ready for the reciprocal withdrawal of lawsuits against Azerbaijan before international bodies once a peace agreement is finalized. Officials outlined the specific conditions under which this withdrawal would occur. Separately, Latvia called for an emergency UN Security Council meeting.

topics.title: Karen Vardanyan donates AMD 122 million to National Gallery renovation
topics.text: Businessman Karen Vardanyan donated AMD 122 million for the renovation, furnishing, and equipping of the Restoration Department at the National Gallery of Armenia. The support was acknowledged by both the Ministry of Culture and the National Gallery.

topics.title: Elmira Karapetyan wins silver at World Shooting Championships
topics.text: Armenian shooter Elmira Karapetyan became world vice-champion, securing a silver medal at the ISSF World Championship. The Armenian women's national football team also learned their opponents for the upcoming Nations League matches.
